analysis.title: The great gold liquidation
key_insights: Gold broke below the $4,000 support on Friday and trades further below its 200-day moving average than it has in a very long time. The first support is the $3,800 area, which coincides with the longer-term trend line.
Gold is oversold, but The Market Ear notes readings can get more extreme in liquidation phases, so oversold does not mean the selling is over.
Gold has hit its 100-week moving average, a level not tested in a very long time. The 200-week moving average sits near $3,000.

Per GS (Quinn), speculative gold selling accelerated during October 20-27 with $8bn of net selling, the fifth consecutive week of outflows. Cumulative selling since September 22 is $19.5bn. Of the latest weekly selling, $5.2bn was long liquidation and $2.8bn was fresh shorts.
Gold fell 1.6% during October 20-27 despite an 11bp decline in US 10-year real yields, which GS reads as a positioning-driven market.

Per GS, Other gross longs remain above their two-year median despite five weeks of liquidation. The risk is that further technical deterioration triggers another wave of selling regardless of falling real yields.
Gold fell another 4.3% between October 27 and 30. Per GS, three-month implied volatility and put skew have risen, with normalized 25-delta put-call skew at the 85th percentile of its one-year range.
Gold has fallen while equity volatility surged, which The Market Ear takes as evidence that gold is not a reliable fear hedge.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Real yields fell 11bp over the week, normally supportive for gold, yet gold fell 1.6%.

risk_factors: Further technical deterioration could trigger another wave of speculative selling regardless of falling real yields.
Gold below its 200-day moving average and through $4,000 support, with a 200-week moving average near $3,000 as a distant level.
Positioning is not washed out, so liquidation may continue.
vol_and_positioning: Per GS, three-month gold implied volatility and put skew have risen. Normalized 25-delta put-call skew is at the 85th percentile of its one-year range.
Per GS, speculative gold selling totaled $19.5bn since September 22. Other gross longs remain above their two-year median, so positioning is not washed out.
Equity volatility has surged while gold fell, so gold has not worked as a fear hedge in this move.
